question: It is claimed in the United States’ National Security Strategy1 that German chemical companies have set up large production facilities in China and are using Russian natural gas there, which is no longer available to them at their European sites. Can the Commission confirm these facts, and if so, why is this the case?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.9.2026) The Commission took note of the US’ National Security Strategy, which is a US internal document not subject to the Commission’s scrutiny. The Commission is not in the possession of data on the energy sources used by chemical plants in China.

However, according to public information, China imports roughly 38 billion cubic meters of Russian pipeline gas annually through the Power of Siberia pipeline, which is used across different sectors and economic actors in the country.

The size of China’s chemical market and its dynamic growth have attracted foreign investment, including from the US, Japan, South Korea, Saudi Arabia as well as Member States’ chemical companies. The Commission has no information on the specific contractual arrangements or feedstock supply of individual industrial plants in China.
